text:
jonah: Ran the nightly perf vs canary — observed a 9% absolute drop in prefix cache hit rate after yesterday's system-prompt formatting change. latency P95 for small-chat routes up ~18ms.

uma: yikes. what changed in the system prompt exactly?

jonah: whitespace + JSON ordering normalization from the UX patch. patch made system prompt insertion deterministic but reordered tool metadata keys.

kevin: repro'd locally. profiler shows more frequent KV misses at token 0 for many requests. totals: hit_rate before=0.72, after=0.63.

perf-bot: nightly-run summary:
 - suite: prefix-warmup
 - baseline_hit_rate: 0.719
 - canary_hit_rate: 0.628
 - delta: -0.091
 - p95_latency_delta_ms: +18.3

ashwin: quick theory: cache key currently includes flattened tool fields in insertion order. any reordering of JSON -> new key.

lisa: we should canonicalize tool metadata ordering + drop volatile fields (session_id, request_id). small change, big impact.

kevin: confirmed. I ran the key-hash for 2k sample prompts: 420 unique keys introduced solely by metadata key-order changes.

jonah: other probs: tokenizer pin mismatch surfaced in a couple of reproducible cases — token IDs differ by 1 for some punctuation, causing different prefixes.

uma: urgent checklist idea:
 - canonicalize JSON field ordering for tool/function metadata (alpha sort)
 - strip runtime-only fields from cache key (session_id, ts, ephemeral_flags)
 - include tokenizer version digest in key (eg. tk_v=sha1)

ashwin: agree. also propose: add a \"len-bucket\" component (short|mid|long) to the key to reduce eviction churn across different prefix lengths.

kevin: re batching heuristics — found that the new key churn reduces effective batching benefits for prefix-serving: smaller effective identical-group sizes -> worse batching -> lower throughput. we saw GPU occupancy drop ~12% during peak.

jonah: sample canonicalizer snippet I sketched:
```json
{"model":"gpt-large","system":"<...>","tool":{"name":"search","params":{"q":"..."}}}
```
Normalized to -> keys alpha sorted inside \"tool\" and top-level, then stringify without extra whitespace.

lisa: we must be careful: some customers rely on rich tool metadata ordering in audit logs. canonicalization should only affect cache-key path, not persisted telemetry.

ashwin: plan of attack:
 1) implement canonicalizer that only runs in cache-key builder (no telemetry changes)
 2) add tokenizer-version tag to key, fallback to baseline if missing
 3) run warmup agent to prefetch top-5k prefixes across regions after deploying canonicalizer
 4) monitor hit_rate and p95 for 48h; rollback if no improvement

uma: on warmup agent: we should avoid stuffing caches with huge cold lists for dedicated customers — limit warmup per-customer to top 200 prefixes and keep TTL short (1h). global warmup OK for hosted routes.

kevin: note on eviction: propose LRU within len-buckets + prefer keep-hot policy for system-prompt-prefixed keys. That reduces cross-talk between short and long prefixes.

jonah: counterpoint: LRU per-bucket increases metadata overhead. we can approximate with segmented LRU using multiple small LRU shards. cheaper to implement.

lisa: regression root-cause RCA: the UX patch changed how tool params were serialized (ordered dict -> regular dict), and a prettier JSON step introduced extra spaces. combined effect changed keys.

ashwin: quick mitigation patch: normalize by serializing with separators=(',',':') and sort_keys=True. will open PR now.

jonah: can we also add a test that computes key fingerprint for sample inputs so future formatting patches fail CI?

kevin: yes — unit test: compute key before/after pretty printer and assert equality for canonicalizable fields. also test tokenizer-version mismatch detection.

perf-bot: action created: PERF-3892 \"cachekey canonicalization + tokenizer pin\" assigned to ashwin, priority: high.

ashwin: PR 5421 opened with canonicalizer + unit tests. leaving experimental flag default=off until we validate warmup safety.

uma: next steps: deploy canonicalizer behind flag to canary, warmup top-5k hosted prefixes overnight, monitor perf-bot metrics. if hit_rate recovers >0.05 absolute within 24h -> flip on; else rollback and deep dive.

jonah: thanks everyone. big lesson: any change to serialization (even whitespace) must be considered in cache key surface. :eyes:
